brief.title: Narrated Video With Zero API Keys
brief.hook: The voice reading this line cost nothing to make. No API key. No account. No cloud.
key_points: Two pip installs — piper-tts and faster-whisper — put narration and transcription entirely on your machine.
One command fetches the voice model; after that nothing phones home.
OpenMontage's tool registry detects both automatically: piper_tts, transcriber, and tts_selector flip to available.
Text in, WAV out — then faster-whisper reads that WAV back with word-level timestamps, which is exactly what the caption burn consumes.
The narration on this video was produced by the commands shown on screen.
brief.core_message: A working narrated-video pipeline is two pip installs away — no API keys, no cloud, no spend.
brief.cta: Clone OpenMontage, run the two installs, and narrate your first video in under five minutes.
brief.tone: matter-of-fact, confident, unhurried — a competent engineer showing you the shortest path, not a product pitch
brief.target_audience: Developers evaluating OpenMontage who have no paid AI provider configured and assume a video tool is useless without API keys

angle_options.name: proof-by-self-reference
angle_options.description: The video's own narration is generated by the commands it demonstrates, and it says so at the close. The demo IS the proof — nothing has to be taken on trust.

angle_options.name: straight-install-walkthrough
angle_options.description: Neutral step-by-step of the two installs and the voice download. Clearer for pure documentation, but no payoff moment and nothing that distinguishes it from a README.

angle_options.name: before-and-after-capability
angle_options.description: Open on the registry showing 0/10 TTS providers, close on it showing piper available and three pipelines unlocked. Strong arc, but spends most of its runtime on JSON output rather than the workflow.

metadata.voiceover_origin: generated (piper_tts, en_US-lessac-medium) — not present in any source recording

critical_moments.why: the entire cost of entry, on one line
the step most people miss; without it piper reports 'Unable to find voice'

critical_moments.shows: piper_tts -> available / transcriber -> available / tts_selector -> available
critical_moments.why: the aha — the system reconfigures itself, nothing to wire up by hand

critical_moments.shows: narration WAV generated, then transcribed back with 8 word timestamps
critical_moments.why: proves the caption path works, not just the voice

metadata.dead_time_note: No source footage means no real dead time. Typing pace is authored via typeSpeed and pause steps, so every frame is deliberate.
metadata.aspect_ratio_rationale: Terminal output lines run long; a 9:16 crop would either shrink the type below legibility or truncate command text. 16:9 at 1080p keeps every command readable at full width.
notes_for_scene_planner: Single continuous terminal_scene for the full 45s — cutting between windows would break the illusion of one session.
Open with a >=2s pause on an empty terminal with blinking cursor before the first character types (synthetic-screen-recording design rule).

Pace commands to narration cues, never ahead of them. Verify with lib/verify_scene_pacing.py before rendering — the documented #1 failure mode is burning through all steps in the first 40% of the scene.
Use pill steps for completion events: 'installed', 'voice ready', '3 tools unlocked'. Max one on screen at a time.
The registry-flip beat is the payoff; give it the longest hold of the video.
Real output text only — every line shown was captured from an actual run in this session. No invented output.
metadata.ep_gate_note: The EP's post-idea check 'if no source footage: STOP' predates this pipeline's synthetic_terminal mode. In synthetic mode there is no capture to assess; the authored steps list is the source, and the manifest lists synthetic_terminal as a first-class production mode requiring only video_compose. Proceeding is correct, not an override.
metadata.cost_note: Every tool in this plan is local: piper_tts ($0), transcriber ($0), video_compose/Remotion ($0), subtitle_gen ($0). No paid provider is reachable on this machine.

decisions.subject: Pipeline for this deliverable

options_considered.label: Screen Demo
options_considered.reason: Deliverable is a CLI setup walkthrough — exactly this pipeline's synthetic_terminal mode, and it needs no image, video, or stock provider.

options_considered.label: Animated Explainer
options_considered.reason: Would work, but wants generated or stock visuals per scene and none are configured.
options_considered.rejected_because: No image generation or stock footage provider available; visuals would degrade to text cards.

options_considered.label: Animation
options_considered.rejected_because: The subject is literal terminal commands — showing them as abstract motion graphics loses the proof.

options_considered.label: Character Animation
options_considered.rejected_because: A cartoon presenter adds production time without making the install any clearer.

decisions.reason: The user picked the OpenMontage setup demo from four offered concepts. Screen Demo's synthetic_terminal mode is purpose-built for install walkthroughs and is fully supported by the currently available toolset.

decisions.subject: Production mode — synthetic terminal vs real screen capture

options_considered.label: Synthetic terminal (Remotion TerminalScene)
options_considered.reason: Every command and its output is already known — they were actually run in this session — so the whole session can be authored to the frame. Deterministic, privacy-safe, and frame-accurate to narration cues.

options_considered.label: Real screen recording (screen_recorder / cap_recorder)
options_considered.reason: screen_recorder and cap_recorder are both available on this machine.
options_considered.rejected_because: The idea-director's test — 'can I predict every command and its output before shooting?' — is yes here. Real capture would also expose desktop content and re-run a 63 MB download live, with no gain in fidelity.

decisions.reason: The demo is a scriptable terminal session whose output is already captured verbatim from a real run, which is the documented trigger for synthetic mode.

decisions.subject: Composition runtime for the final render

options_considered.label: Remotion
options_considered.reason: Owns the TerminalScene component (typed commands, scrolling output, floating pills, blinking cursor) and the word-level caption burn. Installed and verified on this machine.

options_considered.label: HyperFrames
options_considered.reason: Installed and available; excellent for HTML/CSS/GSAP motion graphics.
options_considered.rejected_because: The screen-demo idea-director constrains synthetic_terminal mode to Remotion only — TerminalScene has no HyperFrames equivalent. HyperFrames would be a real choice for a synthetic_ui demo, which this is not.

options_considered.label: FFmpeg only
options_considered.rejected_because: Cannot synthesize an animated terminal; there is no captured footage to concatenate.

decisions.reason: Mode constraint, not a silent default: synthetic_terminal is Remotion-only per the idea-director's runtime table. Both runtimes are installed here, and HyperFrames is genuinely on the table for other briefs — it is not for this one.

decisions.subject: Authoring mode — templated vs atelier

options_considered.label: Templated (stock TerminalScene)
options_considered.reason: TerminalScene is a purpose-built stock scene type carrying pacing lessons from a prior showcase render. A hand-built terminal would re-derive it with more risk.

options_considered.label: Atelier (hand-authored composition)
options_considered.reason: Default for hero and brand work; produces a fresh visual language every time.
options_considered.rejected_because: This is a utility documentation clip, not hero marketing. A bespoke terminal look would cost significant iteration and make the demo less familiar, not more persuasive.

decisions.reason: AGENT_GUIDE reserves atelier for hero work that must impress. A 45-second setup walkthrough is exactly the low-stakes, high-clarity case templated mode exists for.

decisions.subject: Narration TTS provider

options_considered.label: Piper — en_US-lessac-medium (local)
options_considered.reason: The only TTS available on this machine, verified working this session, and thematically the point of the video: the narration is made by the tool being demonstrated.

options_considered.label: ElevenLabs
options_considered.rejected_because: No API key configured; tool reports unavailable.

options_considered.label: Google Chirp3 / Cloud TTS
options_considered.rejected_because: No API key configured; tool reports unavailable.

decisions.reason: Only available provider, and self-referentially correct — the video's claim is that Piper is enough, so it must be narrated by Piper.

decisions.subject: Style playbook

options_considered.label: Clean Professional
options_considered.reason: Recommended for screen-demo; restrained type and contrast keep terminal text legible, which is this pipeline's stated first priority.

options_considered.label: Minimalist Diagram
options_considered.reason: Also listed as recommended for screen-demo.
options_considered.rejected_because: Tuned for diagrammatic explanation; there are no diagrams here, only a terminal window.

options_considered.label: Premium Minimalist
options_considered.rejected_because: Not in the pipeline's compatible list, and its restraint would fight the terminal's own visual identity.

decisions.reason: Legibility before style is the screen-demo operating principle, and this is the playbook the manifest recommends first.

decisions.subject: Background music bed

options_considered.label: No music
options_considered.reason: 45 seconds of dense technical narration; a bed competes with the exact command names the viewer needs to catch.

options_considered.label: Pixabay Music (free, no key)
options_considered.reason: Available with no key and would add polish.
options_considered.rejected_because: The tool scrapes the Pixabay site and can break without warning; a soft bed is not worth a fragile dependency on a first render. Easy to add in a revision if the silence feels stark.

decisions.reason: Clarity over polish for a short technical walkthrough. Reversible — say the word at the assets gate and I will add a quiet bed.
